content.text: In regions where conventional payment processors fail, digital creators face significant barriers in monetizing their content. Countries like Nigeria and Ghana often have limited access to platforms like Stripe and PayPal. COREMERCH addresses this gap by providing a robust infrastructure solution that enables creators to set up a fully operational online store using decentralized tools. This guide details how to utilize Supabase as the order database for your digital store, ensuring you can accept crypto payments without relying on traditional [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/financial-sovereignty-digital-creators-crypto-which-[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/real-[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/real-architecture-behind-selling-digital-downloads-pakistan-stripe-2|COREMERCH guide to architecture]]-behind-digital-product-stores-kyc-payments-13|The Real]]-actually-21|financial]] systems.
Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

The traditional payment landscape is riddled with restrictions, especially in regions facing currency instability. COREMERCH's approach leverages open-source technology and decentralized payment systems, allowing creators to maintain sovereignty over their commerce infrastructure. By using platforms like Supabase and NOWPayments, you establish a resilient backbone for your digital store that inherently avoids the pitfalls of conventional payment processors. This architecture not only circumvents banking limitations but also ensures that you retain full control over your data and transactions.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before deploying your digital store, gather the necessary tools and accounts. First, set up a GitHub account to host your store page. Next, create a Supabase account to manage your order database. You'll also need to register with NOWPayments for crypto payment processing. Ensure you have your digital products ready for upload, whether they are ebooks, courses, or software. Finally, familiarize yourself with the Sovereign Blueprint, which outlines the step-by-step deployment process, specifically for Stack 01, which can be completed in 4-6 hours.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

Begin by configuring Supabase as your order database, creating tables to store customer and order information. Next, set up Google Apps Script to handle backend logic, including integrating with NOWPayments for processing crypto transactions. This setup allows you to track payments in real-time and automate the delivery of digital products. Implement webhooks to ensure your store responds instantly to payment confirmations. This seamless delivery pipeline guarantees that customers receive their purchases immediately upon successful payment, enhancing the overall user experience.
Own your digital store infrastructure without the risks of traditional platforms.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

After you’ve set up your infrastructure, it’s time to go live. Deploy your GitHub Pages site to make it accessible to the public. Conduct thorough testing on the mainnet, ensuring all payment and order functionalities work as intended. Once confirmed, promote your store to your audience. Encourage them to explore your offerings and make their first purchase. Monitor transactions closely to address any issues promptly. This initial transaction is crucial, as it validates your setup and demonstrates the reliability of your infrastructure.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

Once your digital store is operational, focus on scaling. Use Supabase’s features to analyze customer data and optimize your offerings based on purchasing trends. Expand your product range within the existing infrastructure by adding more digital products to your store. Consider employing additional marketing strategies to attract more visitors. Additionally, explore the Edge Commerce Stack offered by COREMERCH, which enhances your setup with advanced features like SPF/DKIM/DMARC configurations and end-to-end testing, all deployed within 48 hours.
How do I build a digital store that accepts crypto payments for free?

The setup sequence matters because each component depends on the previous one being correctly configured. Start with NOWPayments: create your account, configure wallet addresses for each coin you want to accept, generate the API key, and note the IPN secret key you will set. Then configure the backend: in Stack 01, deploy the Google Apps Script Web App and note its URL; in Stack 02, deploy the Cloudflare Worker and note its URL. Set that URL as the webhook endpoint in your NOWPayments IPN settings. Then configure the storefront. Then run a real mainnet test — send actual crypto to your configured wallet address, confirm NOWPayments detects it, confirm the webhook fires, and confirm the delivery email arrives with a working download link.
Streamline your order processing with real-time payment confirmations.

Creators at the store setup stage comparing Stack 01 and Stack 02 are typically choosing between building it themselves with the Sovereign Blueprint at $47 — which covers both stacks in complete detail with full source code — or having COREMERCH deploy the complete Edge Stack under their accounts with the Edge Commerce Stack at $197. Both result in the same ownership structure: your GitHub or Cloudflare account, your Supabase database, your NOWPayments account, your wallet, your store. See both options at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html.
Your Deployment Checklist

Follow the setup sequence without skipping steps — configuration errors are significantly harder to diagnose than setup time. First: create your NOWPayments account, add wallet addresses, generate your API key, and note your IPN secret key. Second: deploy the backend — configure Cloudflare Worker with your NOWPayments credentials and product settings, or configure Google Apps Script with the same — and confirm the endpoint URL. Third: set the webhook endpoint URL in your NOWPayments IPN settings. Fourth: deploy the storefront to Cloudflare Pages or GitHub Pages and confirm product pages and checkout display correctly. Fifth: configure your custom domain and DNS if using one. Sixth: complete a real mainnet test transaction. Seventh: check the order database for the test entry. Only after steps six and seven pass cleanly should you share the store URL publicly.

How do I set up Supabase for my digital store?
To set up Supabase, create an account and configure your database. Set up tables for orders and customer data, and integrate it with your payment processing to streamline order management.
What is the difference between Stack 01 and Stack 02 in COREMERCH?
Stack 01 utilizes GitHub Pages and Apps Script, deployed in 4-6 hours. Stack 02, the Edge Commerce Stack, leverages Cloudflare Pages and Workers for enhanced capabilities and is deployed in 48 hours.
Can I host a digital product store on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages?
Yes, you can host your digital product store on either GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages. Both options provide reliable hosting solutions that are compatible with the infrastructure you need.
How do I process crypto payments without traditional platforms?
Use NOWPayments to process crypto payments. Integrate it with your backend logic, such as Google Apps Script or Cloudflare Workers, to handle transactions without relying on traditional platforms.
